claimed_purpose.text: Multi-tier storage system for persisting conversation history, user preferences, and application data

mechanisms.text: AIRI distinguishes between persistent memory (hard to retrieve, requires semantic relevance and relationship traversal) and working memory (limited capacity), framing the gap as the core problem their memory system addresses.
Two distinct stores are maintained: activeContexts (current live messages per bucket) and contextHistory (a separate history log), distinguishing active message log from historical entries.
A second persistent IndexedDB-backed mount under the key 'outbox', namespaced with base 'airi-sync-queue', suggesting a queued/outbound sync store separate from primary local storage.
Session messages (full turn log including system, user, assistant roles) are the persisted unit — not curated facts. Each session record contains meta and the full messages array.
The chat-sync authority is tied to the main window's route lifecycle and is disposed when the main window leaves the stage route, causing timeouts for detached chat windows
Context prompt construction is delegated to @proj-airi/core-agent, which exposes a ContextSnapshot type and functions for building and formatting a context prompt message.
AIRI uses Character Cards (V2/V3 JSON format) to define persistent personality, appearance, and behavior — representing lore/backstory as opposed to conversational events.
AIRI chose pgvector.rs as the vector database backend for the memory store, citing speed and support for higher embedding dimensions than standard pgvector.
Emotion scores (joy, disgust) are stored per memory entry and are intended to influence retrieval ranking, though not yet fully implemented.
Long-term memory is stored as RAG entries with longer half-lives; higher historical retrieval counts make them easier to recall.
A per-user index of sessions (keyed by userId) is persisted and retrieved separately from individual session records.
Companion personality, memory, and configuration are stored on user's own hardware rather than third-party servers
A devlog entry references FlowChat memory experiments, indicating active memory experimentation as of early 2026.
Three distinct entry kinds — 'note', 'diary', 'focus' — are persisted as curated records, not a raw message log
Full reset of all context state is possible via resetContexts, which clears both active contexts and history.
Default in-memory storage layer created at module load, used as the base storage instance before any mounts.
Memory is grouped with Lorebook, an Alaya layer, and Time awareness as planned but not yet completed work.
Chat session records are stored and retrieved per sessionId under a local: namespaced key in IDB storage.
Memory implemented via a built-in vector database and memory module providing long-term context awareness
Session index is structured per user and per character, with sessions nested under each character entry.
RAG and memory system are called out as sub-projects born from AIRI, alongside an embedded database.
Cloud sync only round-trips user and assistant roles; system, tool, and error roles are not synced.
A separate configuration doc covers conversation memory, context management, and database settings
Memory Alaya is listed as a named WIP sub-system under the Memory roadmap item, not yet complete.
Each soul is a distinct AI agent configured with specific personality traits and knowledge bases
Conversations are stored as full message-array logs in IndexedDB, keyed by ID, with timestamps
Telegram bot requires Postgres (and by implication pgvector) as a backing store for memory
All conversation logs and memory data remain on the self-hosted server
The registry enforces a hard cap of 400 entries on the history log.

ledger.claim: AIRI models memory as having a persistent store and a working memory gap, solved via RAG retrieval into context.
ledger.quote: So there is always a gap between persistent memory and working memory, where persistent memory is more hard to retrieval (we call it recall too) with both semantic relevance and follow the relationships (or dependency in software engineering) of the memorized events, and working memory is not big enough to hold everything essential effectively.
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: AIRI persists chat messages as vector embeddings in a Postgres database (pgvector.rs) with HNSW indexing, supporting multiple embedding dimensions.
ledger.quote: We chose pgvector.rs for vector database implementation for both speed and vector dimensions compatibility (since pgvector only supports dimensions below 2000, where future bigger embedding model may provide dimensions more than the current trending.)
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: AIRI's retrieve policy filters by cosine similarity threshold (>0.5) and returns top 3 results, then re-ranks by combining similarity with exponential time decay (24-hour half-life).
ledger.quote: newer messages will have higher final scores even if their semantic similarity is slightly lower... const finalScore = similarity * calculateTimeDecayScore(message.createdAt)
ledger.label: inferred

ledger.claim: AIRI separates character lore (Character Card JSON: name, personality, scenario, backstory) from conversational memory stored in the vector database.

Memories can be sad, happy - sadness brings negative feedback, happiness brings positive feedback. So this is the part I haven't completed yet.
